question.problem:
$$
{P}_{B\to C}=[\begin{aligned}3 & -5 & 1 \\ -6 & 9 & 0 \\ 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

 

The change-of-coordinates matrix from the basis $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}\}$ to the basis $C=\{{c}_{1},{c}_{2},{c}_{3}\}$ is given above. Find $[x]_{C}$ given that $x=5{b}_{1}-{b}_{2}.$
question.worked_solution:
First, notice that since $x=5{b}_{1}-{b}_{2},$ we have

$$
[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

 

Given the coordinates of $x$ relative to $B$ and the change-of-coordinates matrix from $B$ to $C,$ we find the coordinates of $x$ relative to $C$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\,x\,]_{C} & ={P}_{B\to C}[\,x\,]_{B} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -5 & 1 \\ -6 & 9 & 0 \\ 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}20 \\ -39 \\ 6\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
